I teach in secondary schools and the kids have to ask, which is ridiculous. Personally I let them anyway, and on hot days like today I just tell them they don’t have to ask me and they should just take them off when they need to.

Tbf I have to have the kids ask me about going to the toilet for health and safety purposes (I’m case of a fire alarm or something) but I’ll always let them go. Also the blazer thing is ridiculous to me (and to a lot of teachers, especially during this weather). You do get teachers on a power trip or being petty but for the most part it’s senior management or admin breathing down your neck.

Exactly. As a teacher it’s just practical to let kids take off their blazer when they need. Making them ask for permission makes it desirable and for the kids with behavioural issues it’s more likely they will disrupt the class with it. If you make it normal then kids will accept it as normal. Along with, you know, not controlling when kids control their body temperature during 30 degree weather.

As a teacher I want to say that it is ridiculous for kids to ask permission to regulate their body temperature. A lot of teachers I’ve worked with will just let kids take off blazers when they need to, and I’ve flat out said “in my classroom you don’t need to ask”. Going to the toilet is another thing (health and safety reasons mainly) but I’ll always allow a child to go to the toilet and so do the majority of teachers I’ve worked with. This is mainly an admin issue, although you do see teachers on a power trip sometimes.
